records.name: Stenton, NSCDA/PA
records.summary: The Stenton historic house museum in North Philadelphia, run by the Colonial Dames of America in Pennsylvania. It offers timed house tours, history talks and seasonal family events, such as a fall harvest festival.
records.what_you_do: Book a timed house tour, come to a history talk or a family event such as the Halloween Harvest Festival, or support the Friends of Stenton. Volunteer roles are not listed on the site.

schedule.text: Timed house tours run Tuesday to Saturday from April 1 to December 19, starting on the hour from 1 to 3 pm. Second Saturdays are open 12 to 4 pm, May through October. From early January to March 31, visits are by appointment.

cost.text: Adult admission is $10, and students, children and seniors pay $8. Children under 6 are free, and so are Friends of Stenton members and residents of zip codes 19140, 19141 and 19144. Groups of more than 10 pay $8 each. Some events, such as the fall symposium, have their own ticket prices.

access.notes: The site names these SEPTA options: Wayne Junction station on the Regional Rail, Logan station on the Broad Street Line, and Bus 23, which stops at Windrim and Germantown Avenues.

first_step.how: Book a timed house tour by calling 215-329-7312 or emailing programs@stenton.org. A booking guarantees your place.
first_step.basis: Tours and many events are open to the public and can be booked by phone or email. The site does not describe a newcomer program or say whether walk-ins are welcome.
first_step.what_to_expect: A visit is a timed tour of the historic house that starts on the hour. The site does not say how long a tour lasts or who leads it, so ask when you book. Adult admission is $10, with lower prices for students, children and seniors, and children under 6 are free.
first_visit_tips: Reserve a spot on a timed tour, since a booking guarantees your place.
Arrive a few minutes early, since tours start on the hour.
The gate is on North 18th Street, just off Windrim Avenue.
Take the Regional Rail to Wayne Junction, or Bus 23 to Windrim and Germantown Avenues.

records.notes: Transit names and the reservation wording were checked on the visit page. The page does not say whether walk-ins are welcome, so drop_in is left out, and tier 1's value of true was not confirmed. Tier 1 gave Wayne Junction as about four blocks away; the page gives no distance, so it is not repeated. The site has no volunteer sign-up. Friends of Stenton is listed as a lead.

records.name: Stonewall Sports Philadelphia
records.summary: A recreational sports and social group for the LGBTQIA+ community. It runs leagues in sports such as kickball, volleyball, bowling and pickleball, plus trivia and social events.
records.what_you_do: Sign up for a league as a player, on a team, as a free agent or as a small group, or come to new member mixers and community events.

schedule.text: Leagues run in seasons, with sign-ups before each season. Kickball plays in spring and fall. New member calls and mixers run each season.

cost.text: The league pages do not list fees. The Player Assistance Fund can waive league registration fees in full or in part for people facing financial hardship. Applications open three weeks before each season's general registration.

first_step.how: Subscribe to the newsletter or follow the group on social media, then register for a league on the league registration page when a season opens. Winter 2027 registration is expected to open in mid-November.
first_step.basis: The group runs new member calls and mixers each season and offers free agent teams for people new to its leagues. It does not describe drop-in or first-visit rules, so it is not rated 5.
first_step.what_to_expect: New players can register as free agents, and free agent teams are made up of other new players, so no one arrives with a team. Each season has new member calls to ask questions and learn how leagues run, plus mixers where newcomers can meet people. The site does not list league fees on its pages, so ask before you register.
first_visit_tips: If you do not have a team, pick the free agent option so the group can help match you to one.
Sign up for the newsletter or follow social media so you hear when registration opens.
Email info@stonewallphilly.org with questions about fees or a specific league.
If cost is a concern, look into the Player Assistance Fund before you register.

records.notes: Fall 2026 registration closed August 14, 2026, per the join page. The kickball page gives no day, time, season dates or fee, and the other league pages list no days or times, so the schedule text stays general. Menu-only leagues (billiards, bocce, dodgeball, pickleball) and the wellness programs (yoga, Stonewall In Motion, Stonewall X) were not checked. Two tier 1 wordings ('no athletic experience is needed' and 'monthly updates') were not on the pages read, so they are not repeated. Staff emails found on the pages are not recorded.

records.name: Stories In My Backyard
records.summary: A Philadelphia media arts group that teaches photography, film and virtual reality to Black youth, with Black instructors. It also stages public photo exhibits about Philadelphia's Black music history.
records.what_you_do: Students in the Exposure photography program, which is open to students at predominantly Black middle and high schools, learn photography in a blended format. The group also welcomes teaching artists, subject matter experts and other volunteers through its Take Action page, and visitors can see its outdoor and pop-up exhibits.

schedule.text: Youth programs run through partner schools and libraries, and exhibits and fundraisers pop up through the year. Dates are posted on Instagram, Linktree and Eventbrite.

locations.label: Philadelphia, programs at partner schools, libraries and pop-up exhibits

cost.text: Donations are welcome. Event prices vary: one outdoor event was free, and another suggested a $5 donation for ages 12 and up. Check each listing.

access.notes: The virtual reality parts of the exhibit need in-person headsets, and the online exhibit is best viewed on a computer.

first_step.how: Follow the group on Instagram or open its Linktree to find the next exhibit or workshop and RSVP. To volunteer or offer a skill, send an inquiry through the Contact Us form on the Take Action page.
first_step.basis: Public exhibits and events are posted openly, and the Take Action page lists volunteer roles with a contact form. Youth program seats are for students at partner schools, and the site does not describe a newcomer program.
first_step.what_to_expect: A first visit is usually a public photo exhibit, which may be outdoors, at a pop-up, or online. Some pieces use virtual reality headsets that you can only try in person. Some events are free and others ask for a small donation, and some have required an RSVP.
first_visit_tips: Check the group's Linktree for RSVPs before you go, since some events have required one.
Outdoor events go ahead rain or shine, so dress for the weather.
Plan to visit the exhibit itself if you want to try the virtual reality headsets.

records.notes: Exposure is for students at predominantly Black middle and high schools in Philadelphia, reached through partner schools (PSTV and The Academy at Penn are named on the our-work page). Sign-up steps and the session schedule are not published, so youth program steps are left out of first_step. Youth program cost is not on the site, so cost covers events only. Past exhibit and event dates (2019 to 2025) are not repeated as current. The Eventbrite and Linktree mentions carried from tier 1 were not re-checked.

records.name: Storybook Musical Theatre
records.summary: A children's theatre company that stages family musicals based on fairy tales and classic children's books. It runs a season of shows from winter to summer and also offers theatre classes.
records.what_you_do: See a family musical, take a theatre class, or audition for a show, using the class and audition pages on the site.

schedule.text: Runs a short season of family musicals in several runs from winter to summer. Theatre classes are offered in sessions with their own registration windows.

locations.label: Mandell Campus Theater, Melrose Park (formerly Gratz College Theater)
Giant Community Rooms, Willow Grove (theatre classes)

cost.text: Theatre class tuition for a ten-session fall class is $155 to $180, plus a $20 registration fee that season subscribers skip. Show tickets are sold through the ticket pages linked from the site.

access.notes: The site describes sensory friendly performances, with low lighting, reduced sudden sounds, earplugs and noise-cancelling headphones available, a quiet lobby area, and the option to leave and return during the show.

first_step.how: Register for a theatre class by sending the registration form and emergency contact form with payment, or buy show tickets through the site's ticket link.
first_step.basis: Classes are open to the public by age, with a clear registration step and tuition listed. The audition page linked from the site gave no dates or requirements when read.
first_step.what_to_expect: The fall class meets on Mondays for ten sessions, split into two age groups, and ends with a student showcase at the Mandell Campus Theater in Melrose Park. Registration is not complete until both forms and payment arrive. The site does not describe a trial class.
first_visit_tips: Early registration costs less, according to the class page.
Free parking is available on the theatre grounds and on Melrose Avenue.
Turn into the first driveway on the left off Melrose Avenue, then use the door in the middle of the building.

records.notes: OUT OF AREA. The theatre is at 7605 Old York Road in Melrose Park and the classes meet at 315 York Road in Willow Grove, both in Montgomery County. The mailing address is a PO Box in Abington. No Philadelphia venue or program appears on the pages read, so the verdict is out_of_area. The owner should decide whether a regional children's theatre belongs in the directory; if a Philadelphia venue turns up, this verdict should change. The tier 2 URL /theater-classes returned 404, and the working page is /classes. The audition page was linked but not opened.

records.name: Stray Cat Relief Fund
records.summary: A South Philadelphia nonprofit that traps, neuters, vaccinates and returns stray cats, supplies humane traps to community members who help neighborhood cats, and rescues and adopts out cats from its adoption center.
records.what_you_do: Join the trapping team, or drive cats between outdoor colonies, vet clinics and foster homes. You can also help build or fix shelters on Shelter Build Days, collect food or donations, or foster a cat.

schedule.text: No set hours. Volunteer work fits your own schedule, and Shelter Build Days change with the seasons.

locations.label: Mailing address (P.O. Box 20167), no public meeting place listed

cost.text: Fostering is voluntary and unpaid. The pages checked list no fee to volunteer or foster.

first_step.how: Fill out the Volunteer Application on the volunteer page for the area you want, or email purr@straycatrelieffund.org. To foster, use the foster application linked from the homepage.
first_step.basis: Volunteers and fosters start with an application form. The pages do not describe an orientation or training, or what happens after you apply.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not describe an orientation. Volunteer work ranges from one-time events, such as a shelter build day or a food drive, to ongoing trapping and cat transport. Fostering means caring for one cat at home for an average of 8 to 12 weeks, and the group covers medical care at approved vet clinics with prior approval.
first_visit_tips: Pick the volunteer area you want on the Volunteer page, such as trapping, transport or shelter builds, and use its form.
Fostering needs reliable transport to vet visits and a safe space apart from your own pets.
If you plan to foster, have a short bio and good photos of the cat ready, since the group asks for both.

records.notes: The newest dated items are from 2024 (138 cats given TNVR services, 320 cats adopted), with the year only, so last_sign_of_life cannot be set to a month. The footer year 2023 is not evidence. Status is kept at probably_active from tier 1 because the site and forms are live and no closure is posted, but this is borderline, and a human check before publishing is worth doing. The 'What's happening Meow' news page was not opened. The adoption center's location and hours are not published, so no visit location is given. Tier 1 said the group lends traps; the site says it supplies them, so the summary is corrected. Friends of SCRF is listed as a lead.

records.name: Street Soccer USA Philadelphia
records.summary: A street soccer program with teams in four Philadelphia neighborhoods: North, West, Southwest Philadelphia, and Kensington.
records.what_you_do: Players can join a team at one of the four locations. Coaches and volunteers can apply through a form on the page.

schedule.text: Teams meet at four Philadelphia locations. Ask the group for each team's days and times.

locations.label: Four sites: North Philadelphia, West Philadelphia, Southwest Philadelphia, and Kensington

cost.text: The national site lists no player fees, only donation options.

first_step.how: Email Taz McDermott at taz@streetsoccerusa.org to join a team. Coaches and volunteers can use the Apply to be a Volunteer or Coach form on the page.
first_step.basis: The Philadelphia page names a contact to join a team and a public form for coaches and volunteers. It does not describe a newcomer program or drop-in sessions.
first_step.what_to_expect: The national group says it serves youth ages 4 and up, and also adults, homeless families and people in recovery. The Philadelphia page does not say what a team session looks like or how often teams meet, so ask Taz before the first visit.
first_visit_tips: Email first to confirm the team, day and place you will attend.
Ask what to bring and whether the team has openings.
If you want to help rather than play, the coach and volunteer form is the direct route.

records.notes: The May 28, 2026 Visa and Street Soccer USA post names a planned Philadelphia park, with no address or opening date, and is used as the dated sign of life. A 2024 juvenile justice center kickoff and older 2017 items were not used. The 'youth ages 4 and up' statement comes from the national about page, not the Philadelphia page. No current Philadelphia team calendar was found.

records.name: Street Tails Animal Rescue (STAR)
records.summary: A Philadelphia dog rescue that cares for overlooked dogs in a kennel facility, places them in adoptive homes, and asks for foster homes and adult volunteers.
records.what_you_do: Volunteers walk dogs, help at events, clean kennels, and help with transport. You can also foster a dog, help with events and fundraising, or do photography or content work. Start with the Adult Volunteer Application or the Foster Application on the website.

schedule.text: Office hours are Tuesday to Saturday 11 am to 5 pm and Sunday noon to 5 pm, closed Monday. Visits to dogs are by appointment only, and walk-ins are not accepted.

cost.text: The FAQ lists no fees for visiting, volunteering or fostering.

first_step.how: Submit the Adult Volunteer Application on the website, or the Foster Application if you want to foster, then attend the mandatory 60-minute orientation.
first_step.basis: Volunteers and fosters must apply before they can see the work, and every role starts with a mandatory orientation. Visits to dogs are only for approved applicants.
first_step.what_to_expect: Volunteers commit to at least two shifts or one event each month, and shift lengths are not listed. Volunteers must be 18 or older, have a current tetanus vaccine, and have no history of animal cruelty charges or violent crime convictions.
first_visit_tips: Check that you are 18 or older and have a current tetanus vaccine before you apply.
Plan for the 60-minute orientation, which every role requires.
Visits to the dogs are by appointment only, so call or email before you come.
The page gives no orientation dates, so ask when the next one is.

records.notes: The newest dated item is a 2022 copyright footer, which does not count as evidence, so status stays probably_active from a working site with no dated items (tier 1 decision kept). The 'PFAs' term in the volunteer requirements is not explained on the page and is left out. Foster steps after applying, fostering supplies and vet coverage are not on the pages read. The Adoption FAQ tab content was not captured. The Hound-O-Ween event has no date on the page. Friends of Street Tails is listed as a lead.
